elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 states that HDI assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in the defined “Deliverables,” including materials developed specifically for the Company or the Site.

elements.element: Customer owns all other work product created specifically for Customer.
elements.evidence: The definition of “Deliverables” expressly includes “other materials and work product developed specifically for the Company or the Site.”

elements.element: Vendor assigns all right, title and interest in such deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI “hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest” in the Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 excludes HDI’s pre-existing and generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how from the assignment and states that HDI retains them.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any retained Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence to its retained software, systems, tools and know-how “to the extent embedded in or reasonably necessary to use the Deliverables.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as “perpetual.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly described as “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in all customer, user, order and transaction data collected through or generated by the Site in connection with Deerskin Products, defined as “Company Data.”

elements.element: No joint ownership is created in the intellectual property or data allocated between the parties.
elements.evidence: The clause allocates exclusive ownership through assignment and retention and expressly states that “no joint ownership of any of the foregoing is created.”

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains its pre-existing and generally applicable tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic know-how.
elements.evidence: HDI retains its pre-existing and generally applicable know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives rights in the deliverables equivalent to a licence.
elements.evidence: The Company receives full ownership of the Deliverables through assignment, which is broader than a licence, while embedded retained HDI technology is separately licensed.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The Company’s ownership of the Deliverables and express right to use embedded HDI technology permit business use without a narrower purpose restriction.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership of the Deliverables includes the right to modify them, and the licence covering embedded HDI technology expressly includes modification rights.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership permits the Company to authorize third-party use of the Deliverables, and the licence covering embedded HDI technology expressly includes the right to sublicense.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Deliverables are assigned without a reversion or time limit, and the embedded-technology licence is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is unconditional and contains no revocation mechanism, and the embedded-technology licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment contains no territorial limitation, and the embedded-technology licence is expressly worldwide.

elements.element: Customer’s rights in the deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The assignment imposes no royalty, and the embedded-technology licence is expressly royalty-free.

result.reason: Section 5.5 substantively satisfies the preferred position and gives the Company rights at least as broad as the fallback. However, the redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated terms because it also inserts an unrelated General Manager/bookkeeping and operations provision. That insertion begins as a sentence fragment and materially changes operational governance. The truncated trademark sentence and the somewhat imprecise reference to “any of the foregoing” also reduce drafting quality.
